claims.claim: Sims holds that more examples are better than hedged generalizations when writing a species or culture for a game.
claims.source: Chris S. Sims, Writing: Generalizations and Absolutes, 2020
claims.quote: more examples are better than hedged generalizations

claims.claim: Sims cites the 5e Player's Handbook half-orc passage as superlatives hedged into words doing little work.
claims.source: Chris S. Sims, Writing: Generalizations and Absolutes, 2020
claims.quote: leaving a lot of words doing little work

claims.claim: Sims names Kim Mohan among the mentors who taught him about generalizations, hedging and superlatives.
claims.source: Chris S. Sims, Writing: Generalizations and Absolutes, 2020
claims.quote: Among them is the great Kim Mohan

claims.claim: Teos Abadia records that Season 8 of the D&D Adventurers League moved away from boxed text and separated the information into specific headings.
claims.source: Teos Abadia (Alphastream), The Best and Worst of Adventure Formats at Winter Fantasy 2020
claims.quote: moving away from boxed text and separating information into specific

claims.claim: Abadia records that Season 8 required its authors to use the heading-based format.
claims.source: Teos Abadia (Alphastream), The Best and Worst of Adventure Formats at Winter Fantasy 2020
claims.quote: Season 8 required that authors use the format.

claims.claim: Abadia argues the Season 8 format broke a single place description across several headings so that the door's appearance had to be assembled from two sections.
claims.source: Teos Abadia (Alphastream), The Best and Worst of Adventure Formats at Winter Fantasy 2020

claims.claim: Abadia's verdict is that the Season 8 format actively obfuscates the content and makes the adventure harder to run at the table.
claims.source: Teos Abadia (Alphastream), The Best and Worst of Adventure Formats at Winter Fantasy 2020
claims.quote: actively obfuscates the content and makes the adventure harder to

claims.claim: Abadia praises a rival format's equivalent of boxed text not for being boxed but because it gathers all of the information in one place.
claims.source: Teos Abadia (Alphastream), The Best and Worst of Adventure Formats at Winter Fantasy 2020
claims.quote: eschews the format and actually gathers all of the information

claims.claim: Christopher Perkins, then editor of DUNGEON Adventures, says Warriors of Heaven does not embrace the narrative style of most Planescape products because it is a core AD&D product.
claims.source: Christopher Perkins, interviewed at Planescape: I am the Mimir, 1999
claims.quote: does not embrace the narrative style of most PLANESCAPE

claims.claim: Perkins says that anyone who has edited his work knows he almost always overwrites.
claims.source: Christopher Perkins, interviewed at Planescape: I am the Mimir, 1999

claims.claim: Perkins says an adventure set in Sigil has an entirely different feel from one set in the Abyss, and that he values describing places that could exist nowhere else.
claims.source: Christopher Perkins, interviewed at Planescape: I am the Mimir, 1999
claims.quote: an adventure set in Sigil has an entirely different
claims.page: answer on what he enjoys as a designer

claims.claim: Perkins says the voice and design of the Planescape campaign setting were daring and striking in their originality.
claims.source: Christopher Perkins, interviewed at Planescape: I am the Mimir, 1999
claims.quote: The voice and design of the campaign setting was daring

claims.claim: Steve Winter, TSR's first hire with professional editing experience, says that in games as in journalism the language needs to be direct and clear.
claims.source: Steve Winter, TSR editor, interviewed at Grognardia, 2009
claims.quote: the language needs to be direct and clear

claims.claim: Winter says flowery phrases and clever wordplay are things journalists avoid, and that the same holds in games.
claims.source: Steve Winter, TSR editor, interviewed at Grognardia, 2009
claims.quote: Flowery phrases and clever wordplay are things to avoid

claims.claim: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist, the 2018 city adventure, credits Michele Carter, Scott Fitzgerald Gray and Kim Mohan as its editors.
claims.source: Waterdeep: Dragon Heist (Wizards of the Coast, 2018), credits page, read through the Internet Archive's OCR text
claims.quote: Editors: Michele Carter Scott Fitzgerald Cray, Kim Mohan
